title: Interactive: Who wants what at the COP31 climate change summit - Carbon Brief
gist: Carbon Brief's tracker of party positions for COP31 in Antalya (Australia leads negotiations, Turkey hosts) outlines the main fault lines: operationalising the just transition mechanism, a developing-country push for a climate finance work programme amid donor aid cuts and US pressure on MDBs, stalled adaptation and mitigation talks, and lagging NDCs (150 parties covering three-quarters of emissions).

insights.claim: COP31 has an unusual joint presidency, with Australia leading the negotiations while Turkey hosts the conference in Antalya.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Split presidency may dilute or complicate agenda-setting.
insights.locator: This summit is unusual due to its joint presidency

insights.claim: Carbon Brief analysed around 100 documents to track parties' positions on COP31 issues, ranging from 'priority' to 'oppose'.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Structured position tracker useful for anticipating negotiation outcomes.
insights.locator: In order to track parties’ positions

insights.claim: COP31 takes place against a backdrop of war, energy crisis and climate extremes.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Energy security pressures may compete with climate ambition at the talks.
insights.quote: against a backdrop of war, energy crisis and climate extremes
insights.locator: Delegates will soon gather in the Turkish resort

insights.claim: Key aspects of the Belém-Antalya mechanism for a just transition, agreed in principle at COP30, were settled in June, but many details are missing and parties disagree on its scope and whether it should be tied to finance.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Finance linkage is the key unresolved point.

insights.claim: Civil society groups see getting the just transition mechanism up and running as a key expected outcome of COP31.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff

insights.claim: Developing countries pushed a climate finance work programme onto the agenda to pressure developed countries into more public funding under Paris Agreement Article 9.1, with some proposing a 'burden sharing' arrangement.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: North-South finance tension is likely to dominate COP31.
insights.locator: These parties see this programme as a way

insights.claim: Climate finance talks are occurring as major donors cut aid budgets and the Trump administration pressures multilateral development banks to drop their climate objectives.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Shrinking public finance supply raises the risk of deadlock on finance.
insights.locator: This comes against a backdrop of major donors

insights.claim: Developed countries prefer to focus on improving access to existing finance and broadening the donor base, a stance some developing countries such as small-island states also support.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Pressure for new donors (e.g. large emerging economies) to contribute.

insights.claim: Under the 'Veredas dialogue', countries are discussing Paris Agreement Article 2.1c on aligning all financial flows with climate action, with differing views on what it entails.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Could eventually shape private-finance climate alignment expectations.
insights.locator: Nations have also been discussing Article 2.1c

insights.claim: Parties failed in June to agree details of the global goal on adaptation; after COP30 agreed 59 indicators, these must be refined before COP32 in Addis Ababa.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Adaptation remains a technical, slow-moving track.
insights.locator: Having agreed at COP30 on a list of 59

insights.claim: Developing countries want finance to fund adaptation rather than just track progress, and seek reassurance on last year's pledge to triple adaptation finance.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Adaptation finance pledges are a pressure point.

insights.claim: Negotiators made no progress in June on the mitigation work programme, the only formal agenda item on cutting emissions, disagreeing on whether it should continue or close.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Risk that the formal emissions-cutting track is wound down.
insights.locator: At the June climate negotiations, negotiators

insights.claim: Only 150 parties, responsible for three-quarters of global emissions, have submitted new NDCs covering the period to 2035.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A quarter of global emissions are not yet covered by updated plans.
insights.quote: So far, only 150 parties – responsible for three-quarters of global emissions – have submitted new NDCs.

insights.claim: Iran, Vietnam, Egypt and Argentina are among those without new NDCs, and the US has withdrawn its climate plan under the Trump administration.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: US withdrawal weakens the global ambition baseline.

insights.claim: Global stocktake outcomes such as transitioning away from fossil fuels and tripling renewables by 2030 remain contentious for large developing countries and fossil-fuel exporters.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Fossil-transition language remains vulnerable to rollback.
insights.locator: Some of these outcomes remain contentious

insights.claim: COP31 will launch the second global stocktake, which concludes in 2028.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.locator: COP31 will also see the launch

insights.claim: Turkey's COP31 action agenda pushes global targets for electrification, waste reduction and building-sector emissions, and the Australian negotiating presidency intends a 'cover text' that may capture targets such as electrification.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A global electrification target would be a tailwind for grid and electrification investment.
insights.locator: Turkey will be pushing its “action agenda”

insights.claim: A COP31 presidency 'climate implementation bridge' aims to turn NDC goals into an investable project portfolio.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Potential pipeline of climate projects for investors.
insights.locator: A new COP31 presidency effort dubbed

insights.claim: A joint letter from 105 parties called for COP31 to put the ocean at the heart of climate action by embedding ocean-based action in the UNFCCC architecture.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Ocean-based climate action is gaining formal momentum.
insights.locator: For example, a joint letter signed by 105
